intent: Review the active synchronous-rectifier power-entry construction checkpoint from Atopile through native KiCad and explicit route serialization, preserving known acceptance and qualification blockers.

findings.title: Construction manifest leaves generation-input identity ambiguous
findings.suggested_fix: Partition and hash every generation input (skeleton/native source, libraries, scripts, outline/poses/routes) under explicit generation_input_hashes, and verify those hashes during replay; keep current construction_inputs separate.
findings.first_evidence: source-manifest.json lists construction_inputs and a separate input_hashes set that omits the retained native skeleton, local libraries, and integration/route helpers.
findings.why_it_matters: A changed retained skeleton, library, or helper can produce a different board while the board_sha256 remains unchanged, so the replay identity is not closed.
evidence: source-manifest.json: construction_inputs and input_hashes are separate sets; input_hashes omits native-source-unrouted.kicad_pcb and integration helpers.

findings.title: New exact PCB parts lack required component documentation records
findings.suggested_fix: Add components/<PART>/<PART>_Documentation.md for each newly introduced exact component, or record a scoped exception tying the retained source packet to the component identity.
findings.why_it_matters: The board has exact new controller, MOSFET, fuse, clip, and passive identities, but the repository component traceability convention has no per-part record for them.

findings.title: Route recipe does not establish electrical route qualification
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the serializer transport-only but add/retain a separate Rust/native check for current capacity, voltage-domain spacing, loop inductance and thermal constraints before any acceptance claim.
findings.first_evidence: apply_routes.py:1 -- pure explicit polyline serializer; it does not search routes or judge engineering.
findings.why_it_matters: A clean KiCad DRC result and successful route serialization can still leave high-current, high-voltage, or switching-loop requirements unvalidated.
evidence: apply_routes.py:1 -- pure explicit polyline serializer; it does not search routes or judge engineering.

requirements_completeness.notes: Construction artifacts present; full Rust unit contract and physical qualification remain incomplete.

residual_risks: Rust common suite still rejects the active source entry; native ERC/DRC cleanliness does not close Rust electrical acceptance.
Source/native no-connect representation is documented as 49 compiler nets versus 45 native connected nets and remains outside existing Rust graph comparison.
F2 clip fit, fuse coordination, high-current capacity, surge/common-mode, bootstrap/startup, cooling, and hardware qualification remain open.
testing_gaps: No powered hardware test; no full active-unit Rust validation because the passive contract is intentionally not aliased.
Cross-model review was not run because host privacy review rejected repository egress; in-process adversarial fallback ran.

coverage.peer: Cross-model pass not run: host privacy review rejected external repository-diff egress; local adversarial fallback completed.
coverage.validator: Not run in this bounded subagent receipt; native and Rust evidence were inspected as retained artifacts.
